firstFive.what: A dark two-column money screen: a $52,013.21 balance top left with the nine things it is made of listed under it, and down the right what one coin costs, the last four things that happened, a promise that nothing moves without a click, and a red STOP EVERYTHING
firstFive.who: The person who owns the money and does not trade, checking that nothing bad happened
firstFive.action: Read the balance and leave. When the assistant is asking, the question appears under the balance with YES, ALLOW IT and NO, and that becomes the one action

asked.requirement: Policy and log are clearly collapsible. The control lives in the frame title in the box-drawing register, `[-]` expanded and `[+]` collapsed, and clicking the frame title toggles. Collapsed state persists per panel in localStorage. A collapsed panel releases its flex space to its siblings. The approval gate never collapses
asked.ref: the frame titles are buttons whose text layoutFrames() draws: expanded ends '─────── [-] ─┐', collapsed becomes '├─ POLICY' ... '─────── [+] ─┤', tees instead of corners because there is no body below. Clicking toggles, aria-expanded follows, localStorage carries phosphor.collapse.policy and .log, and after a reload both panels came back collapsed. Space is genuinely released: with four pending proposals the gate body grew 414px to 560px when the log collapsed and all four became visible at once. .panel-gate carries no data-collapse and its frame title is a DIV, so the gate has no control to click

asked.requirement: While the approval gate is disabled, a permanent unmissable line in the gate's own red (#ff3b30): GATE DISABLED - TESTNET - EVERY PROPOSAL AUTO-APPROVES
asked.ref: #gate-banner renders the server's gate.banner verbatim as a 1416px bar at y=43 directly under the status bar, background rgb(255,59,48) with rgb(11,13,11) text: the only inverted block on the page and the only solid field of red. It is not dismissable and has no close control. The APPROVAL GATE frame title also turns red, and the empty gate reads 'no pending approvals: the gate is disabled, every proposal auto-approves'. The client never decides this, driven both ways: with the live payload untouched the bar renders from the server's own gate.banner, and with a stubbed gate {required:true, banner:null} the bar is hidden, body.gate-off is off, the gate frame title returns to green and the empty state returns to plain 'no pending approvals'

asked.requirement: A transaction history tab: actual transactions, swaps, deposits, transfers, clickable from and to addresses to the explorers, gas, value, everything a top-level wallet history shows, interactive

Addresses and hashes are links to the explorer that owns them (etherscan, basescan, arbiscan, solscan, nearblocks, per network). Gas is the receipt figure read back off the chain: 21000 gas at the recorded price, $0.0023, shown to four places so a sub-cent fee does not read as free. Interactive is three things and no more: five filters, a row that expands in place to full addresses, every hash, the gas arithmetic, the venue fee, who decided and why, and links out. No modal and no route, so the one-page rule stands

Four different states, four different words, no blanks

states.basic at 390: Buttons stack, addresses wrap inside their block, price value drops to its own line and its change line follows it left. No horizontal scroll
states.basic what happened populated: Read at 1440 with four real refusals on it from the e2e run. This is the render that caught the zero-priced draft reading 'gathering money of your US dollars (USDT) onto Ethereum', which no test and no audit channel had flagged because every fixture priced above zero. Now 'gathering your US dollars (USDT) onto Ethereum' and covered by a test
states.basic dark resting: 1440x900, 1440x760, 1512x982 and 1920x1080: warm near-black ground, balance top left over the nine wallet rows, price band top right over the log, promise and STOP at the foot of the right column. Page overflow measured at 0px on all four
states.basic dark asking: 1440x900 with a real pending consolidate proposal from /api/mcp: calm bar goes 10px amber and breathes, balance drops to 2.6rem, the question sits under it with four facts and the not-your-wallet destination in full, YES and NO both measured in view, and the wallet below it shrinks to its floor and scrolls
states.basic dark frozen: 1440x900 with the kill switch on: 14px red slab, 'You have frozen everything' in the red field at 4.9:1 on its own wash, the button reads LET THINGS MOVE AGAIN in neutral ink, everything still on one screen
states.basic dark squeezed: 1024x680 asking: the safety valve opens as designed. The left column scrolls rather than the question box, so YES and NO stay measured in view and the wallet heading is pushed below the fold instead of the buttons

driven.how: real pointer input through playwright against the running app at 1440x900, reading CHART.view before and after each gesture, not synthetic events
driven.pan: press, twelve moves, release: panOffset 0 to 23.2 and it holds after release
driven.zoom: wheel in at 30% across: 120 bars to 88.2, panOffset moved 23.2 to 44.2 to hold the bar under the cursor. Wheel back out returns exactly to 120 and 23.2, which is the anchor maths agreeing with itself
driven.price scale: right axis drag switches the scale to manual; double click on the plot returns it to auto and to live
driven.agent: chart_set_view over MCP while the window was open moved it to 5m and 200 bars, and the window followed
driven.race found and fixed: the first pass snapped every gesture back. A refresh fired by the browser's own write landed before that write did, and the browser adopted the stale server view. The rule now: the hand in the window owns the view, the only thing that may move it is the agent, and the answer to our own write is applied from that answer rather than from a refresh
driven.timeAxis: press in the axis strip, eight moves, release, reading CHART.view.barCount either side: right 220px 120 to 202 (squeeze), left 220px 202 to 63 (stretch). The direction is the one the hand expects with the right edge anchored, and it is the opposite of what shipped
driven.squeeze: twelve 280px squeezes in a row: client 2000, server 2000, limits.barCountMax 2000, 2000 candles in the payload. Nothing springs back, because the client reads the ceiling out of the payload instead of restating it
found by looking, not by the audit: The question box rendered EMPTY with two live buttons in it. The hidden attribute is a UA display:none and .basic-ask sets display:flex, which beats it. On an approval screen this is the worst available bug and no automated channel caught it
A black band below the fold: style.css pins html and body to 100% height with overflow hidden for the pro deck, so a scrolling basic document painted the terminal ground under itself

The headline and the warning box were the same sentence written twice. Invisible on the old dense screen, reads as a rendering fault once there is space around it. Fixed in the copy and now covered by a test
Quantity and value were 12px apart and both right aligned, so a dollar holding rendered '1,204.00 $1,204.00' and looked like a duplicated number

A zero-priced draft substituted the word 'money' for the missing figure and produced 'gathering money of your US dollars (USDT) onto Ethereum'. The file already had amountClause for this, which drops the clause instead of wording around it. Every kind runs through it now
driven.price tracker: Polled server-side every 30s into a cache, because buildState is synchronous and every caller depends on that. A failed poll clears the cache rather than leaving the last good figure on screen

firstFivePro.what: A terminal control panel for a crypto wallet held across five chains, with a red bar across the top saying every proposal is auto-approving because the approval gate is off on testnet
firstFivePro.who: The owner of the funds, supervising what a connected AI agent is allowed to do with them
firstFivePro.action: Read the wallet, or click APPROVE/REFUSE when the gate has something pending. With the gate disabled the honest answer is that there is no action, and the red bar is there to say so
